artifex, artificis m.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

artist, master craftsman; author, contriver

The master of an art, as against the mere workman (opifex); with a genitive it names the field, artifex dīcendī (Lewis & Short). Of buildings, see architect.

Other words

  • inventor, inventōris m. — deviser, contriver, inventor

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 3.45: Aristaeus, quī olīvae dīcitur inventor (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The one who thought a thing up, rather than the one who draws it.

  • topiārius, topiāriī m. — ornamental gardener; garden designer

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.5 (M-O s.v. landscape architect) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • dēsignātor, dēsignātōris m. — usher, master of ceremonies

    noun, third declension · avoid · classical · Declension on Wiktionary

    A false friend: the officer who showed people to their seats in the theatre, or managed a funeral (Plaut. Poen. prol. 19; Hor. Ep. 1.7.5) (Lewis & Short).

See also design, design, architect.
